summary: Phase 3 API and data contracts at 8bfb6d1 hold on the happy path: pick-diffs writes model-guide-candidates/1 for the 3.13/3.14 seeding, review-set writes the exact D9 manifest, review-score writes a D13 score file that the Phase 2 guide.ts reader consumes (test R6 asserts the Code review row), adjudicate applies the three verdict words, leak-check matches FR-10, review-prompt.md matches the D10 output block, all five writers require --private with a named exit-2 refusal, and the four required suites pass (21, 13, 16, 15). No Phase 3 commit touches a page or a docs/ file, so the UX browser review does not apply, and plan rows 3.1 to 3.11 with 3.3a and 3.8a are true. One blocker breaks the Phase 4 flow: adjudicate queue/apply and review-score share the id form <diff_id>#F<n>, but the queue takes n from one route's output position while the scorer reads n from the position of the route it scores, so different claims collide on one id and a verdict recorded for one route applies to another route's finding; that breaks D11 per-finding verdicts and changes D13 scores and the rank. One major: the queue match window is 2 lines while D10, its own header, and the Red test header say 3. Four nits cover date validation, uncaught JSON.parse on a malformed key, an inaccurate context-line sentence in review-prompt.md, and CWD-dependent default output folders.
blocking_findings: P3C1-1 [Blocker] review-c: The shared finding id space of adjudicate.ts and review-score.ts does not identify a finding across routes. harness/model-guide/adjudicate.ts:245-269 assigns the id <diff_id>#F<n> from the position of the finding inside ONE route's raw output while deduplicating only by claim (diff, file, line, class, severity, title, reason), and :339-343 writes verdicts[item.id] with last-write-wins; harness/model-guide/review-score.ts:301 reads verdicts[<diff_id>#F<n>] at the position inside the route pass it scores, and :301-304 applies false-claim (minus 2 points), real-defect, and unclear (provisional) from that lookup. Consequence A: two routes whose unmatched findings sit at the same index with different claims produce two queue items with one id, and because each judge file is a flat id-to-verdict map (adjudicate.ts:339-342), the judges cannot give each finding its own verdict, which spec D11 lines 449-452 requires and FR-12 (spec.md:904-912) builds on. Consequence B: a claim reported by route A at index 1 and by route B at index 5 keeps only id F1 (adjudicate.ts:258-267), so scoring route B finds no verdict at F5 and the same claim costs route A two points but costs route B nothing, while an unclear verdict marks one route's pass provisional and not the other's. Both directions change pass scores and the D13 rank that guide.ts turns into the Code review pick (guide.ts:240-285). Neither direction is tested: adjudicate.test.ts:267-311 and :421-437 build multi-route raw only with identical claims, and no test scores two routes against one verdicts file. Rationale: the id form has no route component, so a route-blind queue and a route-local scorer cannot share it. Fix options for Green: give the queue route-neutral unique ids and have the scorer resolve verdicts by claim (file, line, class) instead of position, or produce one verdicts map per route, or make the id carry a claim key. This needs a design decision before task 4.13.
nonblocking_findings: P3C1-2 [Major] review-c: harness/model-guide/adjudicate.ts:81 sets WINDOW = 2 and matchesPlant (adjudicate.ts:161-169) uses first - 2 to last + 2, while the same file's header (adjudicate.ts:24-27), the Red test header (adjudicate.test.ts:32-34), spec D10 (spec.md:435-437), and the scorer (review-score.ts:80 and :221) all define the match window as new_lines[0] - 3 to new_lines[1] + 3. A finding at exactly 3 lines from a plant edge is found by the scorer but queued as unmatched, so judges adjudicate a matched finding and a shared real-defect verdict writes a seeded plant into key.real_defects and into the PM hand-off (adjudicate.ts:344-367). Test J1 (adjudicate.test.ts:303-311) uses line = new_lines[0], so the distance-3 case is untested. Rationale: the queue's own documented contract and spec D10 disagree with the code. Fix: use 3 for the match comparison and keep 2 only for the group window, or correct the header, the Red test header, and D10.

P3C1-3 [Nit] review-c: review-score.ts:82 and :130 accept any YYYY-MM-DD text, including an impossible date such as 2026-02-31, and write it into the score file; guide.ts:172-181 and :252-255 then refuse with input-check: scores exit 2, and preview.sh:156-164 drops the whole six-row overview table. The producer accepts what its consumer refuses. Rationale: one bad --date removes the Code review row and all five other rows. Fix: validate the calendar date in review-score.ts, or let guide.ts skip the pass.

P3C1-4 [Nit] review-c: review-score.ts:268 and :412, and adjudicate.ts:237 and :323, call JSON.parse on a key file and on queue.json with no guard, so a malformed key ends the run with an uncaught exception, exit 1, and a stack trace, while review-set.ts:326-330 refuses the same input with lint: key-json: <diff_id> exit 2 and both headers (review-score.ts:8-9, adjudicate.ts:9-12) promise one refusal line and exit 2. Rationale: the same private input has three different failure contracts. Fix: wrap the parses and refuse with score: key, queue: key, and apply: queue.

P3C1-5 [Nit] review-c: harness/model-guide/review-prompt.md:15 tells the reviewer that a line that starts with a number and a space is a context line, but every body line starts with L (review-set.ts:84 BODY_RE and fixtures/review/sets/mg-2026-11a/src/forge-01.diff line L10 +  const v10 = compute(10);), and a context line is L<n>, one space, the kind space, and the text; lines 12-14 also say each line starts with its new-side number while a removed line starts with L---. Rationale: the D10 input misdescribes the diff format it consumes. Fix: describe the kind character after the number.

P3C1-6 [Nit] review-c: review-set.ts:77 and review-score.ts:75 default --sets and --scores to repo-root-relative harness/model-guide/data/..., but the usage lines (review-set.ts:4-5, review-score.ts:4-6) and every documented command run from harness/, so the defaults resolve to harness/harness/model-guide/data/... which preview.sh:119-142 and update.sh:91-111 never read; a run that omits the flag then writes where no consumer looks and the Code review row stays no pick yet. The Red headers call both flags required (review-set.test.ts:18, review-score.test.ts:20) while the tools make them optional (review-set.ts:196, review-score.ts:138) and no test probes a missing value. Fix: require the flags or resolve the defaults against the repository root.
